prompt:
Paint the COMPLETE top-down map of one floor of a sea-cave dungeon in a fantasy JRPG world as ONE finished game map image, in rich premium modern hi-bit pixel art (hand-placed crisp square pixels, hue-shifted colour ramps, dark warm outlines, lush natural detail), classic top-down RPG map view seen from above with a slight 3/4 tilt (tree crowns, rocks and buildings seen from above with their south-facing sides visible; NOT an isometric view, NOT a diorama, no depth-of-field, no tilt-shift, no 3D render, no perspective).

THE PLACE: THE FIRST FLOOR OF A SEA CAVE, seen from above: winding passages of flat wet dark-grey rock shelves with barnacles, shells and patches of wet sand; channels and pools of dark teal sea water speckled with glowing plankton cross the passages; a round entrance hall in the south opening to the outside at the bottom; a central grotto with a pool and a barnacled standing stone carved with waves and a moon; a west grotto and an east grotto; a passage north to a shelf. Palette: slate and blue-black rock, teal and turquoise water, pale sand, white barnacles, green weed. Echoing, damp, mysterious.

The FIRST attached image is an exact LAYOUT GUIDE drawn on a 48 x 40 tile grid (each tile = 48 x 48 px of the output; the output is 2304 x 1920 px). Trace over it: your painting is laid pixel-for-pixel on top of it and used directly as the walkable game map, so every road, shore, cliff, wall, tree mass, water body and landmark must sit exactly where it is in the guide at the same size (keep every edge within a few pixels of the guide; do not shift, shrink, mirror or re-arrange anything; keep the exact width of the roads and of the one- and two-tile gaps).

The SECOND attached image is only a STYLE REFERENCE from the same game: match its pixel-art rendering (pixel size, clusters, outlines, colour ramps, level of detail). Do NOT copy anything from it (no houses, piers, ships or objects from it).

The guide is soft colour-coding only (its blurred edges only mean the edge is natural and free-flowing): do NOT copy its flat colours, straight tile steps, circles or stripes. Interpret every area as the real material with rich natural variation, and give shores, meadows, rocks and cliffs natural, organic, slightly irregular outlines (bulging or receding by at most a third of a tile around the guide edge). Make it feel like a real, exciting place to explore, full of small natural detail.

Guide colour key:
- light grey-blue with small arcs = the walkable cave FLOOR: flat wet dark-grey rock shelves with barnacles, small pebbles and shells, organic edges (never square or stepped).
- pale beige = patches of wet SAND on the floor (walkable, flat).
- teal = sea WATER inside the cave (not walkable): dark teal water, luminous plankton specks, gentle ripples, a thin wet rim where it meets the rock.
- dark blue = deep water (not walkable).
- grey circles = BOULDERS and heaps of shells (not walkable).
- very dark grey = solid ROCK (not walkable): the cave walls, jagged dark wet sea rock seen from above, their sheer faces showing where they rise above the floor, streaked with green weed and white barnacles; the wall outlines are smooth, rounded and natural like real sea caves: NEVER square, stepped or staircase-shaped, no right angles; everything outside the floors is solid rock.
Landmarks (paint each exactly on its block, at the block's size):
- the blocks in colour rgb(150,150,160) = a waist-high STANDING STONE carved with wave lines and a moon, crusted with barnacles (the tide stone).
Walkable areas must stay walkable-looking: no boulders, trees, fences, crates or objects standing on them unless the guide shows them.

Pixel art rules: crisp square pixels, no blur, no anti-aliasing, no painterly brush strokes, no noise, clear clusters, hue-shifted ramps. Characters in this game are about 72 output px tall, so details should be at that scale.
Lighting: this is the ALBEDO base layer (the game darkens it into night at runtime and adds lamp light on top). Neutral, soft, even daylight-like light as in the style reference; NO darkness, NO night tint, NO long cast shadows, NO light pools, NO glow halo, NO vignette, NO fog over the map, NO clouds over the map.
Do NOT paint any characters, people, animals, monsters, birds, boats or ships on the water (unless a landmark says so), treasure chests, lanterns, lamp posts, torches, campfires, signs, signposts, text, letters, numbers, labels, grid lines, borders, frames or UI. Those are added later as separate sprites: leave the ground open for them.
revised_prompt: Generate ONE complete finished 2304×1920 top-down fantasy JRPG sea-cave floor map image. EDIT/PAINT DIRECTLY OVER THE FIRST ATTACHED IMAGE as the exact pixel-registered layout mask: it is a 48×40 tile map, 48 px per tile. Preserve its walkable floors, nonwalkable solid rock, water, sand, and landmark spatial boundaries to within a few pixels, preserving the narrow passage widths and gaps; never move, flip or rearrange the layout. SECOND attached image is STYLE reference ONLY: match its rich, professional hi-bit hand-placed square-pixel art clustering, details, hue-shifted ramps and warm dark outlines, not its buildings or objects. Map seen directly from above, with subtly visible south-facing wall faces, never isometric or perspective. Exterior of floor network must remain solid cave rock rather than black void. Trace the first guide's organization precisely: south roundish broad entrance chamber opening bottom center, central winding rock passage runs north past two broad horizontal tidal water channels into central grotto, central grotto includes pool east of the passage and a solitary wave-and-moon carved, barnacle-crusted waist-high standing tide stone EXACTLY on the one-tile light-gray landmark square at approximately x960–1008 y768–816. Western grotto at left, eastern grotto at right, north narrow passage ends in upper shelf. Preserve top crosswise teal tidal channels and bottom crosswise teal tidal channels, plus the grotto pools and localized sand patches precisely as indicated. Floors: walkable, flat, wet slate-gray stone shelves, mottled restrained natural variation, fine cracks, shell fragments and sparse white barnacles, green seaweed at borders. Sand patches pale damp beige, flat and walkable. Water dark teal/deep blue with intricate square-pixel ripple clusters and sparse bright turquoise plankton pinpricks but no halos; thin wet rocky rims where water borders floor. Nonwalkable walls and all remaining terrain: continuous massive jagged layered blue-black and charcoal sea-cave rock, nuanced sculpted top surfaces and short darker south faces, seaweed and white barnacles at edges. Natural gently rounded, undulating cave wall outlines, not staircase grids or angular squares. A few nonwalkable boulders only at locations marked for boulders; NO intrusive objects on walkable paths. Organic natural material surfaces rather than flat guide swatches, circles or guide's little arc symbols; eliminate all evidence of layout-guide graphics. Neutral even albedo daylight, readable despite damp mysterious palette, no vignetting, fog, blur, antialiasing or cinematic lighting. Crisp clusters of visible discrete square pixels, at character scale ~72px tall. One seamless whole map edge-to-edge; no grid, framing, UI, writing, characters, creatures, boats, buildings, piers, treasure, torches or signs.
